title: Measured: recapture-stale reported 12/12 changed scenarios as fresh — every screenshot on this branch would have shipped stale
description:
Quantitative follow-up to the 2026-08-12 entry "Astro component scenarios cannot resolve their source". That entry described the MECHANISM (the .astro entity extractor emits only Props, so componentName never resolves to a source file and staleness detection is inert). This entry records what it actually costs, measured on a real feature.

The Full-Bleed Layout feature changed five components — QuoteBand, ExploratoryBand, MorseRule, ActionCard, KochFragment — plus BaseLayout and tokens.css, which every page inherits. A bare `recapture-stale` at the Capture Scenarios step found TWO scenarios to consider and recaptured ONE:

  ▶ 2 scenario(s) to recapture
  ⟲ Unchanged: kochfragment-default — pixel-identical, restored committed bytes
  ⧉ Visual change: morserule-default — 100% of pixels differ

Everything else was judged fresh. Forcing the twelve scenarios whose rendering had actually changed (`--force --target`) recaptured all twelve, each with a real raster diff:

  quoteband-default                58%      home-full-design            15%
  exploratoryband-default          27%      about-full-design           17%
  exploratoryband-without-quote    16%      contact-email-only          15%
  actioncard-default               94%      page-created-from-the-cms   15%
  actioncard-coral-accent          94%      page-minimal-fields         21%
  actioncards-default              89%      page-title-without-body     21%

Every one printed `↳ forced capture of already-fresh target <slug>` first — i.e. coverage asserted fresh on twelve scenarios that were all demonstrably stale. A 12/12 false-fresh rate, including the six APPLICATION scenarios, which suggests the gap is not limited to the component-scenario source-resolution path described in the earlier entry: home-full-design has a pageFilePath and still read fresh after BaseLayout.astro and tokens.css changed underneath it.

Why it matters more than it looks: nothing else in the workflow would have caught this. `visual-components-without-coverage` was clean throughout (the scenarios EXIST, they were just wrong), the audit gate is satisfied by existence, and the Capture Scenarios step's own checklist is satisfied by a `recapture-stale` that exits 0 having done almost nothing. Absent an operator who happens to know which components they touched, this branch ships twelve screenshots depicting the PREVIOUS design, and every downstream reader — the results panel, a PR digest, the next session's baseline — treats them as current. The failure is silent and self-certifying.

`--force --target` is a working escape hatch and its help text is honest about being for "a human who knows a change is invisible to the freshness math". But that is the wrong default for a CSS/layout change, where the blast radius is every page and the agent has to enumerate affected slugs by hand and can silently miss one.

Suggested fix: treat a change to a GLOBAL stylesheet (`stack.json → styling.tokenFile`, and any CSS imported by the root layout) as invalidating every scenario that transitively renders through that layout, independent of the .astro entity-extraction gap. That single rule would have caught all twelve here. Separately, the earlier entry's per-scenario `pageFilePath` pinning remains worth doing for the component half.

Observed on the puzzle-school-rebuild branch.
